Indikator 9 measures a specific healthcare quality or process indicator across Denmark's regions and selected facilities. Based on the available data from 2024, the indicator evaluates whether regions and facilities meet a predefined target or standard. The data reveals a universal failure to meet this target, as every evaluated region and facility is marked as not fulfilling the indicator ("Nej") [^src1]. 

Because the dataset consists of only a single dated section, no longitudinal trends or changes over time can be established. 

When examining the specific achievement rates, the national average for Denmark stands at a mere 1% (10 out of 786 cases) [^src1]. Among the regions, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] performs relatively best with a 4% achievement rate (4 out of 98 cases), followed by [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] at 1% [^src1]. The lowest performing regions are [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]], both recording a 0% achievement rate [^src1]. Private hospitals (Privathospitaler) also report a 0% rate, though based on a very small denominator of 3 cases [^src1].

The clear outlier in this comparison is [[pck-psykoterapeutisk-klinik|PCK, Psykoterapeutisk klinik]], which achieves a 9% fulfillment rate (3 out of 32 cases) [^src1]. Despite being the highest-scoring facility and significantly outperforming the national average and all regional counterparts, it still falls short of the required target threshold, as indicated by its "Nej" status [^src1].
